exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, forceps delivery, cesarean section)
Pelvic floor muscle function (surface electromyography activity)
outcome: Pelvic floor muscle or nerve damage
cohort: The study included 2,462 women who were surveyed 6 weeks after delivery.
finding: Over half of the examined women exhibited LUTS 6 weeks postpartum, with vaginal delivery methods, especially forceps delivery, being key predictors of storage-related LUTS and lower pelvic floor muscle activity.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery (VD) and forceps delivery (FD) were identified as significant predictors of LUTS, and women who underwent VD, particularly FD, exhibited lower surface electromyography (sEMG) activity compared to those who had cesarean section (CS).
